description.text: Giovanni Domenico de Cupis was born in 1493 and entered the Roman Curia at a young age, eventually being elevated to the cardinalate by Pope Leo X in a consistory held on 1 July 1517. His early advancement was largely due to the patronage of Pope Julius II, who had previously fathered a daughter with de Cupis’s mother, Lucrezia Normanni, before she married Bernardino de Cupis, Giovanni’s father.

Throughout his career he held a succession of suburbicarian sees—first Albano in 1531, then Sabina in 1532, Porto e Santa Rufina in 1535, and Ostia in 1537—before being appointed Dean of the College of Cardinals in 1541. He also served as Crown-cardinal of the Kingdom of Scotland and was a close friend of Ignatius Loyola, the founder of the Society of Jesus.

curiosities.text: He served as Crown-cardinal of Scotland, a role that linked the Scottish monarchy to the Roman Curia.
He was a close friend of Ignatius Loyola, the founder of the Jesuit order.
His mother, Lucrezia Normanni, had a daughter with Pope Julius II before marrying his father, making Giovanni a half-nephew of the papal offspring.
He held four different suburbicarian sees in rapid succession, a testament to his influence within the Church hierarchy.
He was appointed Dean of the College of Cardinals in 1541, the highest office among the cardinals.
